findings.current: “H-how could someone as humble as Mr. Jin come all the way to a place this precious?”
findings.defect: “Humble” turns Xiao Shen’s accidental insult into a compliment, weakening Jin’s correction.
findings.rationale: Xiao Shen mistakenly calls Jin 누추한 rather than calling the blood-soaked place shabby.
findings.replacement: “H-how could someone as shabby as Mr. Jin come all the way to a place this precious?”
findings.source: 어, 어떻게 진 선생님처럼 누추하신 분이 이 귀한 곳까지!

findings.current: The combination of the Talullah effect and summertime sentimentality nearly took my breath away. I was relieved to see Xiao Shen, who’d just run over like a sprinter, if only by comparison.
findings.defect: “Talullah effect” leaves the specific awkwardness of having insulted someone’s dead companion inaccessible to readers unfamiliar with the Korean meme.
findings.rationale: 탈룰라 invokes that social blunder; the reference gives the dog exchange its comic sting.
findings.replacement:
The combination of the Talullah[^1] moment and summertime sentimentality nearly took my breath away. I was relieved to see Xiao Shen, who’d just run over like a sprinter, if only by comparison.

[^1]: A Korean internet meme about awkwardly backpedaling after unwittingly insulting someone’s loved one.
findings.source: 탈룰라와 여름 감성이 합쳐지니 숨이 턱 막힌다. 지금 막 단거리 육상선수처럼 달려온 샤오 쉔이 반갑게 느껴질 정도였다.

findings.current:
“So this is what it means to make monsters fight monsters.”

“What are you talking about?”
findings.defect: The draft conveys the tactic but loses Jin’s invented four-syllable idiom and the Skeleton King’s repetition of it.
findings.rationale: The made-up phrase is the immediate subject of the Skeleton King’s question and Jin’s ensuing claim that it is an old idiom.
findings.replacement:
“So that’s *i-mon-je-mon*—monsters against monsters.[^2]”

“*I-mon-je-mon*? What are you talking about?”

[^2]: Jin twists a Korean four-character idiom about using one enemy against another, replacing its middle syllables with “monster.”

findings.current: He was a Grand Mage. And unlike Magic Johnson, a War Mage specializing in combat magic, he was a classic scholar.
findings.defect: Immediately after naming Michael as the suspected killer, “He” can make Michael appear to be the scholarly Grand Mage.
findings.rationale: The source describes Wassmann’s expertise to explain why his hideout would have been protected by barriers.
findings.replacement: Siegfried Wassmann was a Grand Mage—and unlike Magic Johnson, a War Mage specializing in combat magic, he was a scholar through and through.
findings.source: 그는 대마도사다. 그것도 전투 마법에 특화된 워 메이지(War Maje)인 매직 존슨과는 달리, 전형적인 학구파에 속한 대마도사.

findings.defect: Square brackets remain around a title inside a framed System panel.
findings.rationale: The binding Markdown rule uses the System blockquote, not square brackets, to identify panel content.

findings.current: To me, the Main Quest [Cataclysm] was the root I needed to pull out right away. Everything else was just a branch.
findings.defect: The Quest title retains square brackets around a UI term in prose.
findings.rationale: The binding Markdown rule prohibits enclosing UI terms in square brackets.
findings.replacement: To me, the Cataclysm Main Quest was the root I needed to pull out right away. Everything else was just a branch.
findings.source: 내게 있어 [격변]이라는 메인 퀘스트는 당장 뽑아내야 할 뿌리였고, 그 밖의 모든 것은 단순한 잔가지에 불과했으니까.

summary: The draft preserves the main events, but obscures two jokes, leaves a consequential pronoun ambiguous, and retains prohibited brackets around Quest titles.
